design:
D1. Delivery is specified apart from how a conversation looks: attempt counting, give-up, refusal attribution and withdrawal races are backend behaviour with their own tests. Allowance holds pause the queue for a reason outside the Hub and live in provider-allowance-holds.

D2. One turn = one conversation, one kind, admitted by the oldest eligible entry within the hop budget (`inbound_queue.select_turn`, shared by the scheduler and the status route); its depth is the admitting entry's.

D3. Delivery failure: count per entry; at 2 clear the provider session, at 3 withdraw with a reason (`RESUME_RETRY_LIMIT`, `DELIVERY_ATTEMPT_LIMIT`). Provider-named unretryable failures give up at once. Refusals that stop the agent running at all, or block only its own workspace with nothing else runnable, are not counted.

D4. Refusal vs environment: a `TriggerAgentError` marked `request_level` and not transient is the request's failure (status + sentence, input withdrawn); everything else is a wait the input survives. Each answer is attributed to the request's own entries.

D5. Release is unconditional on run end: every terminal path calls `redrain_queued_agents`, independent of whether the bookkeeping after it succeeds. There is no timer.

D6. Every queue write (deliver, withdraw, count, give up) takes effect only if the entry is still queued, so racing writers cannot both succeed.
lifecycle: Split out of agent-conversation-workspace in the 2026-10-08 spec overhaul.
problem: Input that silently stalls, is retried forever, is reported delivered when it was not, or is answered with another request's refusal leaves the operator unable to tell what an agent is doing and an agent wedged behind input that can never run.

requirements.rationale: On Windows an npm `.cmd` shim is executed by cmd.exe, which truncates an argument at its first newline; the Hub unwraps such a shim to the executable it forwards to.
requirements.statement: Every queued input the Hub marks as delivered SHALL reach the agent's model in full, including content spanning several lines; the Hub MUST NOT report an input as delivered when the launch path cannot carry it, and the only change delivery makes is neutralising file mentions in text the operator did not write.

requirements.rationale: A runtime that dies mid-turn is the likeliest failure; a stopped turn and a binding-conflict turn already did what they were going to do, so re-delivering them would repeat work.
requirements.statement: The system SHALL return a failed run's input to the queue however the run failed, keeping its place in arrival order and its conversation, except for a run the operator stopped and a run failed for reporting a provider session other than the conversation's binding; returning input SHALL trigger another delivery attempt without operator action.

requirements.rationale: The agent cannot otherwise tell that half-finished work in its checkout is its own; what to do about it is left to the agent.
requirements.statement: Input delivered after an earlier delivery failed or was refused by the provider's allowance SHALL state, per entry, which attempt this is and that an earlier attempt was cut off before it finished; first deliveries SHALL carry no such note.

requirements.rationale: Taking the minimum let a shallow entry carry a deep one and restart the chain's count.
requirements.statement: An inbound queue entry whose hop depth exceeds the project's hop budget SHALL NOT be delivered in any turn, and a turn's depth SHALL be the depth of the entry that admitted it, never the lowest depth among the entries it carries.

requirements.rationale: A bound with no exit is a wedge; re-basing to 0 records "the operator restarted this chain here".
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL report an entry queued because its hop depth exceeds the budget as held for that reason, and the operator SHALL be able to release it — re-basing its depth to 0, recording the release with the depth it was released from, and scheduling the agent — or discard it.

requirements.rationale: A turn has one workspace, so a mixed batch delivered a turn that was neither.
requirements.statement: Where an agent's queue holds both a review entry and a work entry in one conversation, a turn SHALL carry only the kind of the entry that admitted it (entries naming neither ride with either), and the other kind SHALL stay queued for a later turn.

requirements.rationale: Defence in depth for a caller that hands `queue_entry_ids` to the trigger directly, bypassing the scheduler's narrowing.
requirements.statement: The system SHALL refuse, before any workspace is prepared or process started, a turn whose input asks for both a review and work on a task, or for reviews of more than one task, naming the tasks and stating that a turn has one subject.

requirements.rationale: Answering a refusal as "queued" tells the operator to wait for something that will never happen; answering an environment wait as a failure would discard input the repair is meant to deliver.
requirements.statement: A request submitting input to an agent SHALL be answered as a failure, with the refused condition's own status code and sentence, where the input cannot be delivered because of what the request asked for; input that waits on the environment (no runner bound, CLI missing, workspace not preparable), a turn in flight, or a budget or hold that will clear SHALL be answered as accepted and queued.

requirements.rationale: The turn is built from the oldest eligible input, which may belong to a conversation the caller cannot see.
requirements.statement: Where the system refuses a turn, it SHALL report that refusal only to a request whose own input the refused turn would have carried, and SHALL tell any other request that its input is queued behind other input.

requirements.rationale: A start reported to the wrong conversation is indistinguishable from success; input selection itself stays in arrival order.
requirements.statement: Where a request naming one conversation (the trigger or `POST /conversations/{id}/continue`) causes a turn to start, it SHALL be answered as started only if the turn carried that conversation's input; otherwise it SHALL identify the conversation that did start and say whether the named conversation's input is waiting behind other input, was given up, or had nothing queued.

requirements.rationale: Rendering one confirmation for both outcomes invites a second press that starts a turn nobody asked for.
requirements.statement: The Continue control on a conversation with queued work and no run SHALL distinguish a turn that began in this conversation from one that began elsewhere, naming the other conversation by its title, and SHALL state the server's reason when nothing started.

requirements.rationale: The operator was told synchronously that the request failed; a queue still counting the input would say the opposite.
requirements.statement: Input whose submitting request was answered with a refusal about what it asked for SHALL be withdrawn from the queue with the refusal as its reason and announced as withdrawn (not as given up after attempts); input waiting on the environment SHALL stay queued.

requirements.rationale: A correct status that reaches no readable message has not told the operator anything.
requirements.statement: Where a submission is refused, the interface SHALL present the refusal's own sentence to the operator.

requirements.rationale: Counting the operator's own retries against an agent that cannot run destroys input nothing tried to deliver; where other input could run, the head of the queue really is in the way. When uncertain, the system holds rather than counts.
requirements.statement: The system SHALL NOT count a delivery attempt against queued input where the turn was refused for a reason that prevents the agent from running at all, or where the agent's own workspace cannot be prepared and no other queued input would have run in a different workspace; every other refusal of a turn SHALL count an attempt.

requirements.rationale: Nothing re-evaluates the queue on a timer, and restart reconciliation only examines runs still recorded as running, so a release gated on bookkeeping strands input indefinitely.
requirements.statement: The system SHALL re-evaluate every agent holding queued input in a project whenever a run in that project reaches a terminal status, on every execution path, regardless of whether the bookkeeping after the terminal status succeeds, and a later bookkeeping failure MUST NOT relabel a run that had already ended.

requirements.rationale: An agent with a run stuck in `running` is refused every later turn; a run whose Hub was killed is left to startup reconciliation.
requirements.statement: The system SHALL bring every run whose execution ends inside the process that started it to a terminal status on every execution path without a restart, recording and logging why when it ended abnormally, while still propagating deliberate cancellation.

requirements.rationale: Giving up releases the queue only if something then tries it; counting a rider each time would spend its allowance in one pass.
requirements.statement: Where an attempt to start an agent's turn ends by giving up on queued input, the system SHALL, in the same pass, attempt the input queued behind it, SHALL continue only after a give-up, SHALL count an attempt against any one input at most once per pass, and SHALL answer the request from the attempt that ended the pass (the give-up's refusal where the queue was then empty).

requirements.rationale: A remembered refusal may have stopped being true; presenting it as current contradicts the live state beside it.
requirements.statement: Where an agent's queue status can find no present reason for waiting input and falls back to the refusal of the last delivery attempt, it SHALL present it as "the last delivery attempt was refused: …", except that a refusal naming another agent's turn as holding a task checkout SHALL be checked now and named as the present reason only while that turn still runs; a failed check SHALL still yield an answer.

requirements.rationale: A run that failed before its process started writes no output, so without this the reason sits only on the run's row.
requirements.statement: Where the Hub gave up delivering a message, the conversation SHALL show the message as not delivered with the Hub's reason and, where a run was the last attempt, how that run ended and the error it recorded; it SHALL learn of the give-up on every path, without a reload.

requirements.rationale: A sender told only that its message was sent waits for a reply that the budget will never let happen.
requirements.statement: When a peer message is queued at a hop depth beyond the project's budget, the Hub SHALL record a `queue_chain_suspended` event and SHALL tell the sender, in the send's response, that the message is held by the hop budget.

requirements.rationale: One sentence for every state told an operator whose entry had been given up that it was delivered.
requirements.statement: Withdrawing or releasing a queue entry that is not queued SHALL be refused with a reason naming its actual state — unknown in this project (404), already delivered (naming the run), given up by the Hub (with its reason), or already withdrawn (409) — and releasing an entry within the hop budget SHALL be refused because the budget is not what holds it.

requirements.rationale: A read-then-write let a delivery overwrite a withdrawal the operator had already been answered 200 for.
requirements.statement: Delivering, withdrawing, counting and giving up on a queue entry SHALL each take effect only if the entry is still queued at the moment of the write, so a withdrawal and a delivery or give-up racing for one entry cannot both succeed.

requirements.rationale: The operator is looking at the response; a refusal at spawn would only surface later as a failed or silently unbound run.
requirements.statement: `POST /agent/trigger` SHALL refuse before queueing anything a request it can already tell will never run: an invalid agent name (400), an archived agent (409), a conversation that is unknown, another agent's or archived (409), a `work_dir` overriding a writing agent's isolation (400), a task already decided (409), a review the task cannot receive (409/403), and runtime overrides with no runner bound (409) or that the catalog rejects (400).

requirements.rationale: Each live check describes the agent now; the stored refusal and the attempt count are records of the past and only explain the wait when nothing current does.
requirements.statement: `GET /queue/{agent}/status` SHALL explain waiting input with the first reason that applies, in this order: the agent is running; every entry is over the hop budget; a provider allowance hold; the token budget is spent for autonomous input; the agent is not launchable; the project workspace is unavailable; another agent's running turn holds the task checkout; the last attempt's recorded refusal; and finally the failed-attempt count with attempts left.

requirements.rationale: One failure is routinely a restart or a transient spawn error and must not discard provider-side context; repeated failure suggests the session itself cannot be resumed.
requirements.statement: After an input's second failed delivery, the system SHALL clear its conversation's provider session so the next delivery starts a fresh provider session.

requirements.rationale: One attempt on the old session, one that trips the reset, one on a fresh session; more would wedge an agent across further failing turns before anyone is told.
requirements.statement: After an input's third failed delivery or counted refusal, the system SHALL stop attempting it, withdraw it with a recorded reason, keep the run that last carried it, and report the give-up to the operator as `queue_entry_abandoned`.

requirements.rationale: A refused credential or spent quota fails the same way on every retry, so each retry only spends a run and an error card.
requirements.statement: Where a Copilot turn fails on a root `session.error` whose `errorType` is `authentication` or `quota` and no allowance refusal with a reset ahead applies, the system SHALL count the attempt, withdraw the input at once with a reason naming the failure and stating the Hub did not retry, and keep the conversation's provider session.

in_scope: Delivering queued input intact and in order, and composing a turn of one kind
The hop budget at delivery, held entries, their release, and telling a peer sender its message is held
Counting attempts, re-delivery notes, a fresh provider session after two failures, giving up after three or at once for unretryable provider failures
Refusing at submission what can never run; refusal versus waiting on the environment
Reporting refusals and starts only to the input they concern, and the Continue control's report
Releasing the queue when a run ends; every run reaching a terminal status
Queue status reasons, and how an undelivered message reports its last attempt
Withdrawing and releasing entries, and the race between withdrawal and delivery
non_goals: Which recipient conversation a peer message is bound to: peer-message-routing
Holds caused by a provider's usage allowance: provider-allowance-holds
Which checkout a turn runs in: workspace-isolation
The composer and how the conversation is shown: agent-composer, agent-conversation-workspace

summary: How input queued for an agent becomes a turn. Queued input is delivered intact, in arrival order, one kind (a review or ordinary work) per turn and within the hop budget; failed deliveries are counted, retried on a fresh provider session and eventually given up; refusals and starts are reported only to the input they concern; and held entries can be released or withdrawn without racing delivery.
title: Inbound queue delivery
